content.overview: BNS s. 202 — Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade. BNS restatement of IPC 168. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 168. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 202 is the rule on “Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade”. The section provides that whoever, being a public servant, and being legally bound as such public servant not to engage in trade, engages in trade, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both or with community service. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 202 exists so that “Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade” has a closed legal test in Chapter XII — Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Disobedience, unlawful trade, personation — and a new duty to treat a victim.

The provision in detail
202. Whoever, being a public servant, and being legally bound as such public servant not to engage in trade, engages in trade, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both or with community service
